 Anil Singhvi Market Strategy: Nifty profit-booking zone at 25,375-25,425—Key levels to track
 Written By Sandeep Singh • Published: 8:38 AM, Nov 16, 2026 | Updated: 8:46 AM, Nov 16, 2026 Market guru Anil Singhvi suggests those holding long positions in the Nifty 50 place an intraday and closing stop loss at 24,975 during the November 16 session.
 Zee Business Managing Editor Anil Singhvi expects support for the Nifty50 index to emerge at 25,000-25,100 levels and a strong buy area at 24,825-24,975 levels in Monday's trade (November 16).
 The market guru expects immediate support for the Nifty Bank to emerge at 60,700-60,800 levels and a stong buy area at 60,100-60,375 levels.
 How market guru Anil Singhvi sums up the trade setup 
 Global: Neutral
 FII: Positive
 DII: Negative
 F&O: Neutral
 Sentiment: Positive
 Trend: Positive
 FII long positions at 34.55 per cent vs 37 per cent before the previous session
 Nifty put-call ratio (PCR) at 0.98 vs 1.00
 Nifty Bank PCR at 1.23 vs 1.30
 The market wizard expects a higher zone for the Nifty50 in the 25,250-25,300 band and a profit-booking region at 25,375-25,425 levels.
 For the banking index, he sees a higher zone at 61,300-61,550 levels with a "blue-sky zone" above the 61,765 mark.
 Futures & options (F&O) ban 
 Out of ban: Kaynes Tech
 Already in ban: None 
 New in ban: None
 ANIL SINGHVI MARKET STRATEGY | How to trade Nifty50 and Nifty Bank 
 For existing long positions :
 Nifty intraday and closing stop loss at 24,975
 Nifty Bank intraday and closing stop loss at 60,700
 For existing short positions :
 Nifty intraday and closing stop loss at 25,325
 Nifty Bank intraday and closing stop loss at 61,550
 For new positions in Nifty50 :​
 The best range to buy Nifty is 24,975-25,100 for targets of 25,150, 25,250, 25,300, 25,375 and 25,425 with a stop loss at 24,900 
 The best range to sell Nifty is 25,300-25,425 for targets of 25,250, 25,150, 25,100, 25,050 and 25,000 with a stop loss at 25,500 
 For new positions in Nifty Bank :
 Aggressive traders can buy Nifty Bank in the 60,700-60,800 range for targets of 61,000, 61,300, 61,375, 61,525 and 61,750 with a strict stop loss at 60,600 
 Above the 61,800 level, Nifty Bank is set to be in a blue-sky zone
 Aggressive traders can sell the banking index in the 61,300-61,550 range for targets of 61,000, 60,800, 60,725, 60,550, 60,400 and 60,175 with a strict stop loss at 61,750

 Sandeep Singh 
 Sandeep Singh is a digital news editor with more than a decade of hands-on experience across business, markets, economy and policy reporting, and 15+ years of overall experience in media. His grounding in media began well before he entered a newsroom -- working across script writing, video editing, sound recording and other AV roles that taught him how stories are built layer by layer. He then entered an internship at NDTV, where years on the digital desk shaped his news sense and strengthened the editorial discipline he continues to rely on today.  
 Across his career, Sandeep has handled a wide array of newsroom functions: writing and editing, managing market and policy shifts in real time, spearheading desk roles during high-intensity news cycles, developing content strategy, mentoring younger reporters and working closely with SEO teams to enable wider audience reach. At NDTV, he progressed through various digital desk roles -- reviewing copy, coordinating coverage and running special event shifts during major announcements and market swings.
 At ETMarkets (Times Internet), he expanded his subject expertise further. While managing desk responsibilities, he also wrote in-depth pieces on the commodities sector -- covering everything from global supply-chain disruptions and price-shock triggers to domestic production economics and the downstream impact on consumers and investors.
 His role at CNBC-TV18 Digital marked a new phase: he led the website’s market coverage, guided the flow of data-led stories, curated explainers for volatile market moments, and ensured timely, accurate and context-rich reportage for a digital-first audience. 
 Over the years, Sandeep has built an extensive body of work covering capital markets, economy, commodities, business policy and personal finance -- ranging from rapid response news to deep-dive analytical explainers that help readers understand not just what happened but why it matters. As an editorial leader who has managed teams of journalists, he is particularly passionate about simplifying complexity. His writing philosophy centres on breaking dense financial and policy narratives into clear and meaningful insights for both first-time readers and seasoned market followers. 
 In 2025, he earned a certificate from the USAGM 'Ethical Use of AI for Journalism' workshop, conducted in India by Voice of America and In Old News. The programme covered AI ethics, practical newsroom applications, prompt design, fact-checking AI-generated content, developing AI-guided workflows and creating resilient editorial practices that preserve journalistic value in an AI-driven media environment.   
 Sandeep writes under his full name, maintains a public professional presence and welcomes feedback on his work. He continues to explore how markets, policy and technology intersect -- and how to make those shifts understandable for readers seeking more than just headlines.
